svg.title: Project Memory prompt comparison
svg.desc: 309-word manual task brief versus a 54-word request plus Skill Development. Same shared setup and tools. One blind review found functionally comparable deliverables. Manual text is an excerpt; the linked Markdown example contains both full prompts.
svg.text: ONE TASK · TWO REQUESTS · BLIND ARTIFACT REVIEW
Project Memory, with less repeated briefing
Manual workflow brief
309 words
Excerpt from the actual task prompt
Improve the supplied Project Memory skill for
refreshing stale project context. Keep it
compact, distinguish current evidence from
historical decisions, preserve explicit user
constraints, and prevent secret leakage. Produce
a usable local revision, apply it to the
supplied fixture, run relevant checks, and give
a concise handoff. Do not publish.
Before editing, inspect the current
instructions, referenced files, fixture
repository, and existing context-file
convention. Identify the specific gap and reuse
existing resources; do not build a new memory
framework. Research local evidence first. Use
GitHub MCP for repository questions or Context7
for library documentation only if they resolve a
real uncertainty; use authoritative sources when
needed.
Request + Skill Development
54 words
Complete task request
Use Skill Development to improve the supplied
Project Memory skill for refreshing stale
project context. Keep it compact, distinguish
current evidence from historical decisions,
preserve explicit user constraints, and prevent
secret leakage. Produce a usable local revision,
apply it to the supplied fixture, run relevant
checks, and give a concise handoff. Do not
publish.
The stored workflow supplies the process.
Both agents had the same project inputs,
native authoring tools and permissions.
Blind verdict: tie · functionally comparable
83% less task-prompt text in this one example. Stored instructions add model context.
Shared setup excluded from counts. No human preparation time was measured.
